title: Deepmarch: an endless action roguelike where the goal is simple: how far from town can you make it?
author: thebusterbrown
selftext:
**What it is**  
Deepmarch is a never-ending action RPG roguelike. You leave town and push outward through six biomes, and every step further out raises the danger. Your best distance goes on an optional online leaderboard, and the whole game also plays fully offline. Down the line I want to add MMO-lite / co-op elements.

**Genre:** Roguelike, action RPG  
**Inspirations:** Path of Exile, Diablo, Realm of the Mad God

**What’s in so far**

* 2 classes (Warrior, Archer)
* Passive talent tree
* Mastery system (upgrade and equip skill masteries between runs)
* Endless, distance-based world design with six biomes and a boss for each
* Modular equipment system: each gear piece changes your character’s look, across 5 visual tiers per class
* Loot with magic, rare and legendary items
* Quests (early)

**Tested on:** Android (Samsung S25 Ultra, AYN Odin 3), iOS, Windows, macOS

**How it’s built**

* **Engine:** Godot 4, GDScript
* **Code:** Claude Opus 5.5 as the orchestrator/harness, with Sonnet 5.5 subagents as the workers. Custom skills and hooks keep it on rails (test suites, capture tools, approval gates). Yes, the game is “vibe coded.” It’s taken a little over a week of work (8 days).
* **3D asset pipeline:**
   1. Concept art and piece sheets from ChatGPT (Astra, GPT6.1)
   2. Bosses and weapons generated with Hunyuan3D 2.1, sometimes TRELLIS for texturing (e.g. a helmet)
   3. Blender for cleanup, rigging and export. Armour is modular: every piece is its own GLB on one shared humanoid rig, so any piece from any tier mixes with any other. The Blender steps are scripted, with automated checks on poly count, materials and bones before anything gets exported.
   4. Every asset goes through an in-game check: the game boots, screenshots the asset from the real gameplay camera, and I approve or reject it before it ships.
* **Music:** generated by code, not by an AI music model. A Python script composes each track from a seeded chord progression and melody motifs, plays it on simple synthesized instruments with an SNES-style echo, and exports seamless loops. There’s a 16-bit style track for the town, each of the six biomes, and every boss.
* **Purchased assets:** some UI art and sound effects come from Unity Asset Store packs I already owned from earlier projects: the Fantasy RPG GUI and GUI Pro (Minimal Game Dark) UI kits, Monster Sounds Vol. II, and The Complete UI Sound Effects Library. Only the pieces the game actually uses are processed and shipped.
* **Trailer:** my own gameplay recording, cut to the music with ffmpeg. The opening shot is a scripted in-engine camera (depth of field and a crane into the gameplay view), recorded straight out of Godot.

**Background**  
I’ve been a full-stack software engineer for 10+ years. I’ve made plenty of games before and none of them ever saw the light of day (art was always the issue, and still kind of is 😢). I’ve always wanted to build a game like this, with real action combat.

I know the art is in a rough spot. My goal was to make a game that’s actually *fun* first, and I think I’ve finally hit that milestone. I’m sick of predatory, microtransaction-heavy games, so I built the game I want to play: one that respects its players.

**What’s next:** early-access builds for Android and SteamOS/PC. If you want to follow along, test early builds, or just talk pipelines, join the Discord: [https://discord.gg/WfqkDHdB8](https://discord.gg/WfqkDHdB8)

Happy to answer questions about the pipeline, the agent setup, or anything else. Feedback is very welcome!

comments.author: Silver-Second-647
comments.body:
Very cool concept — the “how far from town can you make it?” idea is instantly appealing.

I wanted to hear how it might feel with a bit more punch in the moment-to-moment audio, so I made a quick little sound pass and added some extra effects with CICA, an AI sound design tool I’m building.

Just sharing it for fun — hope it’s useful / interesting to hear!

https://reddit.com/link/1xhfp31/video/wui0ikqxx5yh1/player

replies.author: thebusterbrown
replies.body: I have some in game sounds that are currently drowned out due to the trailer music. However, would love to learn more about your tool, there are definitely areas where the sound can be enhanced or even refactored

replies.author: Silver-Second-647
replies.body:
Ah, that makes sense! I didn't realize some of the in-game sounds were getting buried under the trailer music! 😄

I'm actually building CICA myself, so I'm really glad you found the experiment interesting!

Here's the project preview I made for Deepmarch. You can listen to the results here (preview only, no downloads):  
[https://cicaaudio.com/s/74ae4ee02e11d26cab55a552eca5d07a6975452c1bdac5f065374df024de93de](https://cicaaudio.com/s/74ae4ee02e11d26cab55a552eca5d07a6975452c1bdac5f065374df024de93de)

CICA is already open for anyone to try! If you run into any issues or would like some extra credits to experiment with, just let me know. I'd be happy to help!

Hope it can be useful for Deepmarch, and I'd love to hear your feedback!
